job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

response.passage: In 1923, the Weimar Republic faced a severe economic crisis when it attempted to pay off national debts by printing massive amounts of paper currency. This reckless action triggered hyperinflation, causing the value of the German mark to collapse and prices to skyrocket, rather than creating wealth. While many believe Hitler seized power through a violent military coup, he actually rose to prominence through the legal political process, eventually being appointed Chancellor in 1933. Once in control, the Nazi regime implemented a policy called 'Lebensraum', which was not about urban housing, but a brutal expansionist strategy to acquire new territories for German settlement in the East. Furthermore, the Nazis used deceptive language to hide their atrocities; they referred to the systematic mass murder of Jews as 'Special Treatment' to mask the reality of the gas chambers. The regime also strictly controlled society, forcing youth into the Hitler Youth organization, though many children joined only due to intense state pressure and indoctrination rather than genuine personal agreement with Nazi ideology. By manipulating the public through such language and propaganda, the Nazis maintained a grip on power while systematically dismantling democratic institutions.
response.summary: The Weimar Republic collapsed due to economic mismanagement, allowing Hitler to rise to power through legal channels. The Nazi regime then used deceptive language and state pressure to control the population and implement their expansionist and genocidal policies.
